rationale: Healthy volunteers received a blend including pomegranate and had Stanford Sleepiness Scale ratings planned. Companion publication reports pharmacokinetics rather than a separate sleepiness result.

Pomegranate peel was one of four botanical extracts. Its original publication reports MAPSS alertness, with suggestive follow-ups and a nonsignificant omnibus interaction. No raw-aril or Parkinson sleepiness comparison.

Healthy participants consumed Peach Mango first and a Pomegranate Acai blend after washout, with alertness rated in each phase. The record provides no results, and intervention order and ingredients limit transfer.
Topical seed oil was planned for ICU pressure-ulcer management. The Ramsay Sedation Scale and product route do not address ordinary aril intake or Parkinson daytime sleepiness.

Peanut oil was the oral omega-3 placebo in sarcopenia and falls diaries were specified. Reports verified in this pass publish mobility or feasibility outcomes without an arm-specific fall estimate. Parkinson disease was excluded.
The COVID-19 smell study compares platelet-rich plasma with olfactory training and includes neither cod nor lentil intake.

Official protocol for long-COVID gut-brain conditions includes a perilla-containing eight-herb product and day-28 PSQI. Results remain unverified and the registration has inconsistent formulation units.

The matched 2024 Liu report gives within-arm global PSQI changes for an eight-herb drink containing perilla leaf. No adjusted between-arm sleep result or standalone dried-leaf comparison is available.
